deals.headline: Lansdowns convert £7.5m of club debt into Bristol City Holdings shares
deals.summary: Bristol City Holdings allotted 7,500,000 ordinary shares for £7.5m by way of a debt-to-equity swap with its parent Pula Sport Limited, funding the club's £7.5m cash requirement for the year; Ashton Gate's £1.0m need was met by an interest-free loan from Pula Sport. Companies House SH01 filings show similar annual allotments (e.g. capital GBP 197,706,262 after 30 June 2025).

notes: Financial figures come from the Bristol City Holdings Limited group accounts, a scanned Companies House PDF: evidence strings were transcribed from the page and a text search of the PDF will not find them. The group consolidates the club, Bristol City Women and Ashton Gate Limited (the stadium business), so revenue is group turnover, not the football company alone. Revenue by class (not summed here, because the accounts' classes do not map one-to-one onto matchday/broadcast/commercial): matchday £3,437,862; season tickets £3,968,343; broadcasting £825,300; Football League pool £7,198,107; solidarity payment £5,340,000; other football income £1,933,787; other commercial and retail £17,634,418. The £4.4m Bristol City Women proceeds are from the strategic report ('The sales proceeds amounted to £4.4m'). Companies House: Bristol City Holdings has filed a statement since 13 May 2025 that it has no registrable person (its parent Pula Sport is in Guernsey). August 2026 reports (Sky News, BBC) of talks with George Daskalakis, co-founder of Betano owner Kaizen Gaming, over a stake: unconfirmed, so not recorded as a deal. Stadium capacity uses the club's own figure (26,389); Football Ground Guide gives 27,000. Not found: valuation, social follower counts, honours.

owners.evidence: The ultimate controlling parties are Mr and Mrs S Lansdown.
owners.name: Steve and Maggie Lansdown (via Pula Sport Limited, Guernsey)

ownership_summary: Steve Lansdown (co-founder of Hargreaves Lansdown) and his wife are the ultimate controlling parties: Bristol City Holdings Limited, which owns Bristol City Football Club Limited and Ashton Gate Limited, sits under Pula Sport Limited and ultimately Pula Limited, both in Guernsey, within the wider 'Bristol Sport' group. Lansdown has put almost £300m into the club and funds it by converting intercompany debt to equity. In August 2026 Greek gaming entrepreneur George Daskalakis was reported to be in talks to buy a stake; no deal had been announced.
